findings.title: Dimension and pressure ranges confined by the description to the superelastic convoluted seat ring but claimed generally
findings.attack: [0088] and [0091] state that the ranges 'correspond to the superelastic seat ring (30) with a convoluted wall (32)' and are to be adapted for polymer, resilient metal, other geometries, wiper rings and larger bores; claims 67 (independent, no material), 76/77 (PEEK) and the dependent range claims apply them to all of those. Art 84 lack of support over the claimed scope; 'seat ring wall thickness' is defined only for a convoluted wall yet claimed via claim 8.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Ask the inventor whether the ranges hold for PEEK, resilient metal and other geometries; if so, add that statement, remove the self-limiting sentences in [0091], [0146], [0161], and redefine seat ring wall thickness in [0028]. If not, narrowing is the only route: claim 67 takes 'formed from a superelastic alloy' and claims 76/77 lose the claim 67 ranges (scope given up: polymer or plain-metal seat rings of the claimed dimensions).

findings.title: Illustrated purge gap cannot open by the outward deflection described
findings.attack: The description says the illustrated seat ring (and the wiper ring) deflects radially outward and thereby opens a purge gap between its outer surface and the core body bore; outward movement of an outer surface closes that clearance. [0103] itself says the gap opens only where the outer surface moves away from the bore. The FIG. 1 instruction draws a clearance there in the closed state, contrary to claim 1's 'purge gap ... closed'. Insufficiency and clarity objection against the only built embodiment and claims 29/30/72.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Obtain the inventor's statement of the built mechanism; rewrite [0020], [0040], [0053], [0054], [0093], [0162] and the FIG. 1, 3, 6, 10B instructions to it, keeping [0103]-[0106] as alternatives; remove the closed-state clearance from FIG. 1. No claim narrowing.

findings.title: Load path and purge exit of the illustrated embodiment cannot be reconstructed from the text
findings.attack: The poppet opens chamber-ward ([0046]); the purge shoulder is on the chamber side of the sealing face ([0038]); the seat ring is seated against the internal shoulder at the end opposite the sealing edge ([0079]) which [0116] places on the chamber side; the purge gap is the outer clearance with the interference band at the internal shoulder ([0036], [0053]) and the flow leaves to the chamber side ([0056], [0059]). The text never names the surface of the ring on which the shoulder bears, and describes no exit from the outer clearance past the interference band and the internal shoulder for the illustrated embodiment. [0105] and claim 31 put a purge gap on the chamber side of the sealing edge along the poppet stem although [0088] has the stem in the ring bore; [0116] has a chamber-ward moving part bearing on the seated chamber-side end. The FIG. 6 instruction calls the interference-fit/purge-gap convention a drafting assumption, not a confirmed mechanism. No drawing exists to resolve it.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add disclosure in [0038]/[0052] of the ring surface that receives the axial load and its axial position relative to the sealing edge and the seated end; add in [0056]/[0059] where the purge flow leaves the outer clearance in the embodiment of FIGS. 1 to 4; reconcile [0079], [0105] and [0116]; give the FIG. 3 and FIG. 6B instructions the same contact location and exit. No claim narrowing.

findings.title: Numerical ranges disclosed only for the superelastic convoluted seat ring are claimed with every alternative material, wall form and valve format
findings.attack: [0088], [0091], [0094], [0146] and [0161] state that the ranges of [0089]-[0090] are those of the superelastic seat ring with a convoluted wall and are to be adapted for a polymer ring, a resilient-metal ring, another wall geometry, a wiper ring and a larger bore. The 'any one of claims' dependencies claim those ranges with claims 9, 24, 51, 52-53, 57 and 76-77, and claim 82 attaches them to a method reciting no material or wall; claim 16 on claim 8 alone drops both the wall and the material. Intermediate generalisation and added matter at the EPO; written-description objection in the US.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add disclosure stating which parameters are fixed by the bore and poppet and apply to every material and wall form (inner diameter, outer diameter, free length on the face of [0088]) and which are set by the threshold-setting arrangement (crack pressure, over-travel threshold, over-travel distance), and give conceived ranges for polymer and resilient-metal rings. If the inventors cannot confirm, narrow: make claims 13, 16, 17, 35, 41-44 depend on claims 11 and 47, claims 69, 70, 78 on claim 73, and add the material of claim 47 to claim 82; scope given up is the numerically limited fallbacks for the polymer, resilient-metal, wiper-ring and Schrader embodiments.

findings.title: Stated axial layout does not bring the purge shoulder into contact with the seat ring
findings.attack: The poppet opens towards the chamber side, lifting the sealing face from the sealing edge; the purge shoulder is 'on the chamber side of the sealing face' and so moves away from the sealing edge; the seat ring bore admits only the poppet stem. Nothing places any part of the seat ring on the chamber side of the purge shoulder, and the text never states which end carries the sealing edge or which surface the shoulder meets. The reader cannot reconstruct a working arrangement from the words.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add an inventor-confirmed closed-state layout paragraph giving the axial order of internal shoulder, seat ring ends, sealing edge, sealing face, purge shoulder and poppet head, the face of the ring contacted and the main-passage route; correct [0021], [0038], [0112] and claim 3 together if 'chamber side of the sealing face' is wrong.

findings.title: 'Seat ring wall thickness' in claim 16 is defined only for a convoluted wall
findings.attack: Claim 16 depends on claim 8 without claim 11 and so covers plain, frustoconical, slotted and cellular walls (claims 5, 15), but [0028] defines the seat ring wall thickness as the radial thickness of the material forming the convoluted wall; for other walls the term has no referent, and [0075] says a resilient-metal ring is given a thinner wall.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add to [0028] a definition of seat ring wall thickness for walls without convolutions (radial thickness measured at a portion free of slots, cells or flare).

findings.title: [0009] invites US means-plus-function construction of the genus terms
findings.attack: [0009] tracks the statutory 112(f) wording (corresponding structures and their equivalents) for deflecting formation, threshold-setting arrangement, deflectable ring element and biasing member; the nonce-like terms are likely to be confined to the described structures and their equivalents, undoing the functional genus, with an indefiniteness exposure if the link to structure is judged unclear.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Rewrite [0009] to state each is a structural term with the listed species as non-limiting examples and delete the 'corresponding structures ... and their equivalents' wording; counsel to confirm no 112(f) treatment is intended.

findings.title: Drafting commentary in the figure plan and instructions must not reach the drawings or the brief description
findings.attack: The figure plan and figure instructions contain internal references (Prompt 20 Assumption A2, 11.md, 14.md, Gate 2, 01 Q1/Q2, DA- and CB- codes) and statements of doubt ('not a confirmed mechanism', 'the inventor states doubt about pursuing it', design-arounds 'not drawn' because they need new matter); the FIG. 6 instruction asks for a footnote symbol on the sheet referencing that assumption. The package has no brief description of the drawings, so these instructions are the only source for one; any carry-over is an admission.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Strip all internal references and statements of doubt or assumption from the figure instructions, delete the FIG. 6 footnote instruction, and write the brief description of the drawings from the description text.

findings.title: FIG. 1 instruction draws the purge gap open at rest, against claim 1 and [0040]
findings.attack: The FIG. 1 instruction says the purge gap is shown as a closed zero-width line and also that the remainder of the seat ring outer surface is drawn with a small clearance to the core body bore even in the closed state. A drawing showing a clearance at rest is the opponent's exhibit that the purge gap of claim 1 is not closed and that the purge flow path is open in the normal-open state, and is an added-matter trap if cited as basis.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Correct the FIG. 1 and FIG. 6A instructions so the free portion is drawn in contact with the bore at rest, or add disclosure in [0036]/[0040] that a running clearance exists but is closed to flow at rest by a stated feature.

findings.title: Inner-surface purge gap not shown to be separate from the main passage
findings.attack: The main passage route is never described beyond 'past the sealing face'; in [0105] the purge path runs along the poppet stem through the seat-ring bore, the clearance being 'closed, or ... sufficiently small to carry no significant flow' in the normal-open state, while the main passage then carries full flow by an unstated route. Separateness required by claim 1 is asserted, not shown; 'no significant flow' is relative.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the main-passage route for the illustrated embodiment and the third arrangement and show how the two paths differ; replace 'no significant flow' with a statable criterion.

findings.title: Multiple dependencies create combinations the description excludes or makes incoherent
findings.attack: Claim 24 with claims 8, 16 and 17 contradicts [0096] ('no separate seat ring'). Claim 34 with claim 29 contradicts [0110] (the flutes open by movement away from the bore). The NiTi-derived ranges (claims 13, 16, 17, 35, 41-43, 67 applied to 76-77) read with a polymer, resilient-metal or wiper-ring element, where [0091], [0094] and [0146] say the ranges must be adapted. This raises Art. 84 and US written-description objections.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Prune dependencies: claim 10 on claims 1-4, 6-9; claim 34 excluding 29; claim 29 excluding 6; claim 23 over-moulding only for a polymer core body; claim 24 on claims 1-7, 10-15; claims 47-50 excluding 24; claim 99 on claims 67-75 or 78. No supported scope lost.

findings.title: Package labels the interference-band arrangement an unconfirmed drafting convention
findings.attack: The FIG. 6 instruction and registry flag 3 state the axial-band interference fit is 'not an asserted inventor fact' and instruct a footnote on the sheet; if filed, the application itself disclaims the inventor's conception of claim 21's feature, raising entitlement and inventorship questions.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Obtain inventor confirmation and delete the footnote instruction and flag 3; if not confirmed, delete claim 21 and the corresponding passages of [0036], [0053], [0103], [0133], [0151].

findings.title: Single-rate spring with ring-stiffness threshold not shown to keep the ring at rest in the normal-open state
findings.attack: Per [0122] the deflecting formation loads the ring before the threshold ('initial elastic rise' before the plateau), so the ring is not 'in its at-rest form' throughout claim 1's normal-open state; for polymer or plain metal the threshold is 'less distinct', leaving no defined state boundary.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add inventor-confirmed disclosure that sub-threshold elastic loading leaves the purge gap closed and define 'at rest' in [0010] accordingly; alternatively restrict claim 40 to claim 47 (scope given up: polymer and plain-metal rings with a stiffness-set threshold).

findings.title: 'Defined wiping edge' undefined in the claim and disclosed only for the laser-cut seat ring
findings.attack: [0127] discloses a 'sharp-cornered edge set by the cut profile of the seat ring' preserved by limited electropolishing; claim 27 drops 'sharp-cornered' and extends it to any ring element, including stamped wiper rings and moulded PEEK rings where neither step applies; 'defined' has no measurable boundary.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Define 'defined wiping edge' in the definitions section and, if the inventor agrees, state that it may be provided on a wiper ring or moulded ring by the forming route.

findings.title: [0160] cross-refers to a background section that is not in the package
findings.attack: [0160] refers to 'the failure modes described in the background'; the package has no background, title, field, summary, brief description of the drawings or abstract, so the reference dangles.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Supply the front sections and check the cross-reference, or reword [0160] to cite the definitions at [0024] and [0029].

findings.title: Claim 10 on claim 5 combines an axial-load conversion wall with a radially loading formation
findings.attack: Claim 10 recites conversion of an axial load; claim 5's tapered purge shoulder applies a radial load and [0113] says the ring 'need not' have a conversion geometry with it; the combination is permitted by silence, never described as working.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add to [0113] that the tapered purge shoulder may also bear axially on a ring having a conversion wall, if conceived; otherwise make claim 10 depend on claims 1 to 4 and 6 to 9.

findings.title: Claim 29 'radially outward' on claim 6 conflicts with the ovalising deflection of the lugs
findings.attack: [0054] treats ovalising as a sense distinct from radially outward and [0114] says the ring moves outward at the loaded points and inward between them; claim 29 on claim 6 is open to a clarity objection and a construction that 'radially outward' means uniformly outward.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add to [0054] or [0114] that an ovalising deflection is radially outward at the loaded arcs within the meaning of the description.

findings.title: Claim 84 claims a compressed-gas device producing over-travel that the description says may not occur
findings.attack: [0179] says compressed-CO2 devices 'may or may not' exceed the over-travel threshold and only the floor pump was tested; [0073], [0100] and [0171] say chilling by such a device may impair the shape recovery that is the last step of claim 79.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Counsel to weigh whether claim 84 earns its place; if kept, add to [0058] the over-travel threshold band intended for a compressed-gas device, if conceived.

findings.title: Limitations supported only implicitly in the claimed combination
findings.attack: Wiper ring 'carried by the core body' (claim 1 with 9) and retained against the internal shoulder (18 via 9); 0.03 mm interference for a polymer ring (20 with 52); wiper ring wiping 'the sealing face' (26 via 9); 'carried by the valve stem through the core body' (59); convoluted wall on seat ring 730 (63); check 'during the pressing' (102) - each rests on general statements, not a direct passage.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add one explicit confirmatory sentence for each combination in the relevant paragraph.

findings.title: Wording drift and package defects bearing on support
findings.attack: Claim 1 'not exceeding' vs [0043] 'below'; claim 1 'to its at-rest form' vs [0013]/[0014] 'towards'; claim 58 uses (30) for the stem-carried ring registered as 730; [0160] refers to a background section absent from the package; no Brief Description of the Drawings; figure instructions carry internal working references and the registry states description and claims do not exist.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Align [0043] to 'does not exceed'; align 'to'/'towards'; use (730) or no numeral in claim 58; supply or re-point the background reference; strip internal references from the figure instructions and refresh the registry.

findings.title: Structural fallbacks (retention band, outer-clearance purge gap) rest on a retention and flow geometry the description does not complete
findings.attack: The interference band and internal shoulder are at the seated end, the outer clearance is the purge gap, and the flow is said to reach the chamber side without any stated route past the band and shoulder; the FIG. 6 instruction calls the convention a drafting assumption. An amendment to claims 21 or 30 will be read with that gap in view and refused as not a derivable working combination, or granted and attacked for insufficiency.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add to [0036], [0053] and [0059] an express description of the band, the free portion and the route by which the purge flow leaves the outer clearance to the chamber side, and match the FIG. 3 and FIG. 6 instructions to it.

findings.title: Face of the seat ring on which the purge shoulder bears is never stated
findings.attack: [0038] and [0052] say only that the purge shoulder 'bears on the seat ring'; [0116] implies the illustrated contact is not at the remote end but never states where it is; no fallback narrower than claim 4 on load location has basis.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add, with the inventor's layout, a sentence stating the face or region of the seat ring contacted by the purge shoulder and its relation to the sealing edge and convolutions.

findings.title: Fixed-seat and wiper-ring fallback has no geometry, dimensions or retention of its own
findings.attack: [0093] leaves the wiper ring's form, thickness and retention to follow from the material; [0162] is prophetic; the FIG. 10 instruction lists no internal shoulder or retention; whether the wiper ring wipes the sealing face is never said. Every step past claim 9 rests on [0094] 'applies to both' and the genus at [0132].
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add to [0093] the wall form, retention means and location, wall thickness range if conceived, and the poppet surface crossed on recovery for the spring-steel wiper ring; add the internal shoulder and retention to the FIG. 10 instruction.

findings.title: Interference band disclosed only for the seat ring, only optionally, and flagged as unconfirmed
findings.attack: The band is disclosed for 'the seat ring 30' only; extending it to the wiper ring and to crimp or sleeve retention relies on [0094]'s general equivalence statement, an intermediate-generalisation target; the figure instructions call it 'not an asserted inventor fact'.
findings.least_narrowing_action: After inventor confirmation, add a sentence that for any deflectable ring element, including the wiper ring, retention may act over an axial band adjacent the locating formation, leaving the deflecting portion free of the bore.

findings.title: Multi-feature fallbacks rest only on the generic combination statement of [0143]
findings.attack: Fallbacks selecting one species from each of several lists (deflecting formation, wall, purge-gap location, flow path, threshold arrangement, material, retention) rely on [0143]'s blanket 'disclosed in combination with each of the others'; at the EPO this is commonly given little weight for multi-list selections, and only [0145] states specific combinations.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a short 'preferred combinations' section on the model of [0145], stating in terms the combinations of amendment paths 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8 and 10.

findings.title: Nested range tiers are separate lists, not linked to each other or to rings other than the NiTi convoluted seat ring
findings.attack: Each parameter has its own three-tier 'in some embodiments' list; combining intermediate tiers of two parameters is a selection from two lists, and [0006]'s sub-range boilerplate does not disclose the combination; all tiers are tied to the superelastic convoluted seat ring.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add sentences stating the intermediate tiers together and the narrow tiers together, for dimensions and for pressures/strokes, and record the inventor's answer on other materials.

findings.title: No coherent embodiment gives basis to amend to an outer-surface purge gap with flutes
findings.attack: The only basis for the outer surface moving 'away from the core body bore' is [0103]'s 'may be' list, while the illustrated-embodiment passages describe outward deflection; an examiner can refuse the amendment as not disclosed as a working embodiment.
findings.least_narrowing_action: After inventor confirmation of the mechanism, add an end-to-end paragraph for the illustrated embodiment covering the outer-surface gap, direction of movement, uncovering of flutes (362) and the free portion left by the interference band.

findings.title: No statement of what closes the drawn at-rest clearance to flow
findings.attack: The FIG. 1 instruction draws a small clearance at the free portion of the outer surface in the closed state while claim 1 and [0040] say the purge gap is closed; the description does not say what closes that clearance to flow at rest.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Draw the free portion in contact with the bore at rest, or add to [0040] the feature that closes the clearance to flow at rest.

findings.title: No basis for an amendment reciting recovery speed, force or the audible snap
findings.attack: [0077] disclaims any speed or force qualifier and [0158] says the audible snap is not a measurement; the natural distinction over closing-stroke wipers has no numerical or qualitative basis in the text.
findings.least_narrowing_action: If a recovery time or force has been measured or can be bounded, add it to [0063] or [0098] with its conditions; otherwise rely on the material limitation of Path 5.

findings.title: Wipe of the sealing face not stated to occur for every one-piece seat ring material
findings.attack: The sealing-face wipe is described for the NiTi seat ring; for PEEK [0063]/[0124] say only 'a surface of the poppet', so a material-free sealing-face wipe fallback may be treated as generalised from the NiTi example.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a sentence that in every one-piece seat ring, whatever its material, the sealing-edge region moves across the sealing face during shape recovery, if the inventor agrees.

findings.title: [0009] invites means-plus-function construction of the functional genus terms in claim 1 and claim 36
findings.attack: 'Element', 'arrangement' and 'formation' plus function, with [0009] reciting 'corresponding structures ... and their equivalents', supports §112(f) treatment confining claim 1 to disclosed species and equivalents; if not invoked, the 'any structure capable of' sentence supports a written-description attack on the functional genus.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Redraft [0009] to rely on the structural definitions at [0014], [0021], [0022], remove the 'corresponding structures and equivalents' formula and state that means-plus-function treatment is not intended.

findings.title: Disclosed but unclaimed alternatives: US dedication risk and literal escape
findings.attack: Claims 1, 58 and 79 require the poppet itself to over-travel at a pressure differential above the threshold, and claim 1 requires the ring to be carried by the core body. The separate purge actuator [0123], depressor-only over-travel [0066] (natural in a Schrader core, [0137]), the inverted arrangement [0117] and deflation-only purge [0067] escape literally, and in the US may be dedicated to the public.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Reformulate the purge-state limitation of claim 1 as the poppet being movable beyond the normal stroke into over-travel, with the pressure-differential trigger dependent; or add an independent claim in which a deflecting formation moved by the poppet or by a pressure-responsive purge actuator produces the radial deflection; add dependent cover for [0117]; decide on [0142].

findings.title: Evidenced technical effect belongs to the wipe, not to the purge gap that distinguishes claim 1
findings.attack: The only data show fouling in the purge-gap region and clean surfaces where the ring wipes; the effect of the distinguishing feature over the admitted conventional core is unproven, the problem is reformulated as an alternative bypass, and a secondary passage opened later in a poppet stroke is CGK.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add any observation of the purge flow path surfaces, or purge-only/wipe-only data if it exists, or an explanation in [0169]; keep claims 25-26 as fallback; do not narrow claim 1.

findings.title: Four disclosed alternatives fall outside claim 1 and are dedicated to the public in the US
findings.attack: Purge on every opening with no normal-open state ([0051]), a separate purge actuator with the poppet on its normal stroke only ([0123]), the inverted ring-on-poppet arrangement ([0117]) and deflation-only purge ([0067]) are described, unclaimed and excluded by claim 1; a competitor cites the applicant's own description.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add an alternative independent claim without the normal-open-state requirement on [0051] and a claim to the purge actuator on [0123]; counsel to decide on [0117] and [0067].

findings.title: Illustrated embodiment's purge gap described as opening by outward deflection against the bore, contradicted by [0103] and the figure instructions
findings.attack: An outward-moving surface cannot move away from the rigid bore surrounding it; [0103] and [0110] say the outer-surface gap opens by inward or ovalising movement, the FIG. 1 instruction states both zero-width and small clearance at rest, and the registry records the FIG. 6 mechanism as a drafting assumption; the only built embodiment is not coherently taught.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Added disclosure stating which surface bounds the purge gap in the illustrated embodiment and in which sense it moves, with [0020], [0053], FIG. 3, FIG. 6B and the FIG. 1 instruction aligned to it.

findings.title: Preferred embodiment: outward deflection is said to open a gap at the outer surface
findings.attack: An outward-moving outer surface reduces its clearance to the core body bore, so the described mechanism of the only built embodiment and of Example 3 is not credible as written. The registry calls the FIG. 6 convention an unconfirmed drafting assumption and draws a clearance at rest, contradicting a closed purge gap. No route for the purge flow past the sealed interference band at the internal shoulder is described. Claim 1 survives on [0054], [0103] and [0106], but the tested embodiment, claim 30, and claims 29 and 30 together face insufficiency and Art. 84 attack.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Obtain the actual P-1 to P-3 mechanism (moving surface, sense, gap location, bypass of the retention band) and rewrite [0040], [0053], [0093] and the FIG. 3, 6 and 10 instructions to match, amending 'outward' in the illustrated embodiment if the movement is inward or ovalising. A description correction; claim 1 is not narrowed.

findings.title: Rule 43(2) and unity: claims 67 and 90 do not share the purge-gap feature with claim 1
findings.attack: Three independent product claims plus two methods; claims 67-78 and 90-102 recite no purge gap, over-travel or threshold, so a posteriori they share no special technical feature with claim 1 once a convoluted thin-walled ring or the standard laser-cut/shape-set route is found.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Narrowing is the only in-application route: add the superelastic alloy and a link to the sealing-and-purging function to claim 67 and make claim 90 recite that ring, or divide claims 67-78 and 90-102 out; scope given up is the polymer seat ring per se and the generic route.

findings.title: US multiple-dependency structure is improper and the claim set is fee-heavy in all three offices
findings.attack: Multiple dependent claims depend from other multiple dependent claims (37 CFR 1.75(c)); five independent claims and 102 claims attract excess and multiple-dependency fees in the US, claim fees above 15 and 50 at the EPO, and excess-claims fees above 25 at the UK IPO.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Prepare a US claim set with single dependencies and a fee-budgeted EPO/UK set, keeping displaced dependents as fallback text in the description; no scope change.

findings.title: Austenite finish temperature claimed without a measurement method
findings.attack: Af depends on the measurement method (DSC or bend and free recovery) and none is stated: EPO Art. 84 unusual parameter; US 112(b) indefiniteness issue; UK s.14(5)(b); a competitor can choose the method to avoid infringement.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the measurement method and standard actually used for the prototype seat rings.

findings.title: Blanket statements will not secure an amendment basis at the EPO or in the UK
findings.attack: Under Art. 123(2) and s.76, amendments that select from several lists of alternatives or create new range endpoints are judged on direct and unambiguous disclosure; blanket statements such as [0006] and [0143] are not, as we understand practice, accepted as that basis.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add explicit fallback paragraphs for the combinations likely to be needed in prosecution, each drawn from existing content, instead of relying on [0143].

findings.title: Breadth of the functional genus against the demonstrated contribution
findings.attack: Claim 1 covers every material, geometry, gap location, threshold arrangement and format; only one NiTi species was tested, the purge and the wipe were not separated, and the purge region was found fouled. EPO: effect not credible across scope, problem reformulated as an alternative (Art. 56). UK: Biogen/Regeneron breadth insufficiency. US: full-scope enablement, lower risk in a mechanical art.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Obtain data separating purge from wipe and a PEEK build before filing or within the priority year; make sure fallback claims 47, 11 and 25 each stand as problem-solution positions. No narrowing of claim 1 proposed.

findings.title: Claim 46 and claim 31 each contradict a limitation of claim 1
findings.attack: With a depressor the gap does not close when the pressure falls, so claim 46 lacks claim 1's closing feature; in claim 31 the supply side reaches the inner-surface gap only through the open main passage, against 'separate from the main passage ... from the supply side'.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Reformulate the closing clause of claim 1 as occurring when the poppet load on the ring is removed ([0060], [0098]) and reformulate claim 31 to say the purge gap communicates with the supply side through the open main passage and is distinct from it ([0105]).

findings.title: Claim count, multiple dependencies and independent claims in one category
findings.attack: 102 claims; claim 10 and many others are multiple dependent claims referring to other multiple dependent claims (US 112(e), 37 CFR 1.75(c)); multiple-dependent and excess-claim fees; EPO R. 43(2) objection likely to independent product claims 1, 58 and 67 and claims fees from the 16th claim; UK excess-claims fees above 25.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Restructure into singly dependent chains for the US; justify claims 1, 58 and 67 as interrelated products or fold claim 1 into claim 58 through claims 59-61; prune to the intended fallback ladder.

findings.title: Claims 25 and 80 are defined by a result on sealant
findings.attack: Claim 25 defines an apparatus by a result on sealant film, which is not part of the claim (EPO result-to-be-achieved, Art. 84); whether a ring that rides over the film infringes is uncertain, and the shearing result is not measured.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recast claim 25 kinematically (a portion of the ring moves across and in contact with a surface of the poppet during shape recovery) and keep the shearing effect in the description.

findings.title: Clarity terms likely to be objected to in all three offices
findings.attack: 'associated with', a 'closed' gap, 'at-rest form' defined by an unclaimed purge shoulder, 'shears sealant film', 'about' with no tolerance, 'nominally', 'low-adhesion', 'tyre set-up', 'surfaces on which sealant film accumulates', 'verified on sampled seat rings'.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Reformulate each using existing description text without changing scope, as set out in the finding.

findings.title: Description lacks formal sections, refers to an absent background, and the figure files carry drafting-process content
findings.attack: No title, field, background, summary or brief description of the drawings; [0160] cites 'the background' which does not exist; the figure plan and registry cite prompt numbers, DA codes, sketch filenames and an assumption footnote to be placed on a drawing sheet.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the missing sections using existing text; strip every internal reference from the draftsperson instructions; remove the FIG. 6 footnote instruction.

findings.title: No relationship between over-travel distance, convolution amplitude and recoverable strain; key values never measured
findings.attack: The skilled person is not told how much over-travel the ring absorbs or what strain results; [0088] says the numbers follow from relationships it does not give, and [0091] admits the over-travel distance and gap opening were design values not measured.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the design relationship used, or state that the over-travel stop limits the axial load on the ring in the worked example.

findings.title: Numerical dependents claimed in combinations the description says were not derived for
findings.attack: Ranges derived for the superelastic convoluted seat ring are claimed with the wiper ring, polymer, resilient-metal and non-convoluted species while [0091] says only that the skilled person will adapt them; support, enablement and later added-matter exposure.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add to [0091] that the ranges apply as starting values to the other species and how they are adjusted; failing that, make the numerical dependents depend on claim 11 or claim 47 (narrowing).

findings.title: Purge gap associated with the deflectable ring element is vague
findings.attack: Associated with states no physical relationship; EPO Art. 84, UK s.14(5)(b) and US 112(b) attacks are available, and the examiner can read the claim on any gap that opens when some ring moves.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Replace with a purge gap bounded at least in part by, or formed through, the deflectable ring element, co-extensive with [0102]-[0107].

findings.title: Ranges the description ties to NiTi with a convoluted wall are claimed without that limitation
findings.attack: The description says the ranges correspond to the superelastic convoluted seat ring and must be adapted for polymer and other forms, yet the range claims are open as to material and geometry; claims 76-77 read with claim 67 claim a PEEK ring at the NiTi ranges. EPO Art. 84, UK s.14(5)(c), US written description.
findings.least_narrowing_action: If the inventor confirms the ranges hold across materials, amend [0088] and [0091]; otherwise make the range claims depend on claims 47/73 and 11, which gives up range cover for polymer and resilient-metal rings only.

findings.title: Required description sections are missing; [0160] refers to a background that does not exist
findings.attack: No title, technical field, background art, problem or summary, brief description of drawings or abstract (EPO R. 42(1), R. 47; US 37 CFR 1.74, 1.72(b)); [0160] refers to failure modes described in the background, which does not exist.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the missing sections, including an acknowledgment of background art, and supply or reword the background that [0160] relies on.

findings.title: Sufficiency across the breadth of the functional genus of claim 1
findings.attack: One built species supports a genus of every material, geometry, gap location and deflecting formation, each non-built combination left to adaptation; UK s.14(3) and Art 83 breadth attack.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add starting values for the polymer seat ring and the wiper ring and state which geometries suit which material class; no claim narrowing.

findings.title: Terms of degree whose tolerance [0007] expressly disclaims
findings.attack: Claims use about, approximately and nominally while [0007] says these define no tolerance: EPO Art. 84 objection likely, and deleting the word narrows to the exact value; US reasonable certainty after Nautilus; UK s.14(5)(b).
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recast claim 44 on the disclosed sub-ranges 0.91-1.09 bar and 3.2-3.8 bar ([0090]); for claims 20, 101, 49, 75 and 98 obtain a tolerance band or specification range from the inventor or supplier.

findings.title: Unity: three groups of independent claims
findings.attack: Claims 67 and 90 need no poppet, over-travel or purge gap; their only shared feature (a seat ring with a convoluted wall converting axial load into radial deflection) may be known per the index summary of ref #1. US restriction likely; EPO R. 64/164 further search fees; UK s.14(5)(d).
findings.least_narrowing_action: Keep claims 1, 58 and 79 in the parent and plan divisionals for 67 and 90, as amended per F-32-4 and F-32-5.

findings.title: Figure instructions carry drafting annotations and text for the drawing sheets; reference-sign use
findings.attack: The figure instructions cite internal working ids and would put a footnote flagging an unconfirmed assumption and long sentences on the sheets (EPO R. 46(2)(f), US 37 CFR 1.84); numeral 30 is attached to the genus in claims 1 and 58; numeral 34 is reused for the fixed seat's sealing edge.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Strip internal annotations, limit sheet text to short labels, drop or widen (30) after deflectable ring element, and give the fixed seat's sealing edge its own numeral.

findings.title: Numeral and preamble mismatches
findings.attack: Claim 58 uses (30) for the stem-carried ring numbered 730; claims 100-102 recite valve-core assembly under a seat-ring manufacturing preamble; [0142] is an unclaimed 'separate concept'.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Claim 58 '(30, 730)'; retitle claims 100-102 as a method of manufacturing a valve core; mark [0142] as not part of the claimed invention.

findings.title: Claim 67 (seat ring): a known wave ring plus routine dimensions
findings.attack: Claim 67 recites no poppet, over-travel, gap or material; for a valve core limits only to suitability. Index #1 is summarised as a NiTi wave-section ring giving radial displacement. The remaining dimensions are, by the description's own admission in [0088], routine consequences of the parameter relationships.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Narrowing required: add superelastic alloy with Af below 5 C and a continuous sealing edge (gives up polymer and resilient-metal rings as components), or recast as the matched kit of [0141] (gives up the bare-ring claim); check #1's full text first.

findings.title: Claim 90 (manufacture): standard NiTi processing applied to a known ring form
findings.attack: Laser cutting NiTi tube on a mandrel, shape-setting in a fixture around 500 C, quenching and electropolishing is common general knowledge for NiTi components; claim 90 departs only in the product, which F-32-4 shows is weak; no process effect is asserted.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Narrowing required: tie the method to the product features that survive F-32-4, or to making the valve core of claim 1 (combining claims 90 and 100 with claim 1), giving up seat-ring manufacture outside such a core.

findings.title: Claim 90 is the standard superelastic NiTi tube-processing route
findings.attack: Laser cutting NiTi tube, shape-setting in a constraining fixture with heat and quench, and electropolishing are the standard route; the sealing edge and convoluted wall are the shape set, not process features.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Make claim 90 recite manufacture of the seat ring of amended claim 67 and add the press-in step of claim 100; narrowing.

findings.title: Every independent claim ties the purge to over-travel of the poppet caused by the pressure differential
findings.attack: Depressor or hand over-travel [0066], a separate purge actuator with the poppet on its normal stroke only [0123], and Schrader cores opened by the head pin [0137] all fall outside claims 1, 58 and 79; claim 57 describes a combination a competitor would not build; if F-32-2 shows depression, the tested embodiment is outside the claims too.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Define the purge state by the poppet or a deflecting formation moving with it being beyond the normal stroke, with the pressure-differential trigger and mechanical depression as sibling dependent claims; or add an independent claim with a deflecting formation driven by the poppet or a pressure-responsive purge actuator.

findings.title: Figure plan and registry contain drafting-process content and a self-contradictory FIG. 1 instruction
findings.attack: Prompt numbers, DA codes, sketch filenames, 'no image has been seen', 'the inventor states doubt', and an instruction to footnote an assumption on a drawing sheet; the FIG. 1 instruction cannot be drawn as written.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Strip every internal reference from the draftsperson instructions, delete the FIG. 6 footnote instruction and state one at-rest condition for FIG. 1.

findings.title: Purge-on-every-opening and separate purge actuator disclosed at [0051] and [0123] and excluded by every independent claim
findings.attack: A single-rate spring with the shoulder engaging the ring from the start of the stroke, or an annular piston purge actuator with the poppet on its normal stroke only, is outside claim 1's normal-open state and poppet-driven deflection; the competitor cites the applicant's own description.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add an alternative independent claim without the normal-open-state requirement on [0051] and a claim to the purge actuator on [0123].

findings.title: The test evidence does not show that the pressure differential drives over-travel
findings.attack: With a floor pump the differential across the poppet should fall between strokes and go negative on removal, yet the snap was heard only on removal. That is at least as consistent with the pump head holding the poppet in over-travel ([0066]) as with the claimed pressure-driven mechanism. How a 3.5 bar differential develops across an open main passage is not explained, and travel was not measured.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Obtain the pump head type, whether it bears on the poppet, whether a snap occurred between strokes, and any measurement of differential or travel; add that disclosure and correct [0044], [0068] and [0158].

findings.title: Background, field, summary and brief description of drawings missing; [0160] dangling
findings.attack: Required sections and the abstract are absent; [0160] refers to failure modes described in a background that does not exist, in the paragraph reporting the comparison on which the effect rests.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the missing sections with an acknowledgment of the saved background art, and supply or reword the background that [0160] relies on.

findings.title: Carried by the core body, read with [0005] and [0117]
findings.attack: Read with [0005], a poppet-mounted ring is indirectly carried by the core body, which widens the prior art that reads on claim 1; [0117]'s contrast lets a defendant using the inverted arrangement argue it is excluded. Scope is uncertain either way.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recite a deflectable ring element carried by one of the core body and the poppet and a deflecting formation carried by the other, with the core-body-held arrangement dependent.

findings.title: Claim 1: the technical effect is not credibly shown, which opens a combination attack
findings.attack: Claim 1's only claimed effect is the air purge, which the data do not isolate and which did not clean the purge region; the problem may be reformulated as an alternative second flow path, with index #16 or #14 (two-threshold second paths) combined with #1 (radially deflecting NiTi ring). Motivation is thin, hence medium.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add data isolating the air purge before filing or within the priority year, state the effect of the separate purge path explicitly, and keep claims 25 and 47 as fallbacks.

findings.title: Claim 31 inconsistent with claim 1's 'separate from the main passage ... from the supply side'
findings.attack: In claim 31 the supply side reaches the inner-surface gap only through the lifted sealing face, so the purge flow path is not separate from the main passage from the supply side.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Reformulate claim 31 to state the purge gap communicates with the supply side through the open main passage and is distinct from it.

findings.title: Claim 46 omits the closing feature of claim 1
findings.attack: With a depressor holding the poppet in over-travel the gap does not close when the pressure differential falls, so claim 46 lacks a limitation of claim 1.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Reformulate the closing clause of claim 1 as occurring when the load applied by the poppet to the ring is removed.

findings.title: Clarity terms in claims 1, 44, 49, 55, 64
findings.attack: 'associated with', a 'closed' gap, 'at-rest form' defined by an unclaimed purge shoulder, 'about' with no tolerance, 'nominally', 'low-adhesion', 'tyre set-up'.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Reformulate each from existing description text without changing scope, as set out in objection 14.

findings.title: Closing the purge gap when the differential falls below the over-travel threshold, versus hysteresis
findings.attack: Superelastic unloading hysteresis, and spring friction, can keep the gap open until the differential is well below the threshold at which it deflected; a defendant argues the closing condition of claims 1 and 58 is not met literally.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Replace with closing the purge gap as the pressure differential falls, as claim 79 already words it; no loss of scope.

findings.title: Convoluted wall being defined by the laser cutting
findings.attack: A convolution is a radial excursion of the wall; laser cutting a tube does not by itself displace the wall radially, so that alternative is not enabled as recited, and Example 1 never says which step formed the convolution.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Record which step formed the convolution in Example 1, and delete by the laser cutting from claim 90 or explain how a cut profile defines the convolution.

findings.title: Inverted arrangement and deflation-only purge disclosed and excluded by claim 1
findings.attack: The ring-on-poppet arrangement and deflation-only purge are described, unclaimed and outside 'carried by the core body' and the pressure-differential purge state; dedicated or argued as deliberately excluded.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Counsel to decide whether to claim on [0117] and [0067] or leave unclaimed.

findings.title: NiTi-derived ranges claimed for every material and geometry
findings.attack: The description ties the ranges to the superelastic convoluted ring and says they must be adapted for other forms; the claims, including a PEEK ring in claims 76-77, assert them for every form.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Amend [0088] and [0091] if the inventor confirms the ranges hold across materials; otherwise make the range claims depend on claims 47/73 and 11.

findings.title: Result language on an unclaimed material in claims 25, 79 and 81
findings.attack: Shearing and carrying sealant film are results on a material not part of the claimed article, and 'surfaces on which sealant film accumulates' depends on use.
findings.least_narrowing_action: 'so as to shear sealant film, when present'; name the purge flow path surfaces by structure in claim 79.

findings.title: Shears sealant film is a result to be achieved
findings.attack: The apparatus is defined by an unmeasured effect on a material outside the claim; whether a ring riding over the film infringes is unclear; against index #3's closing-stroke wiper rings, the distinguishing point is the recovering ring itself, which the claim should recite.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recast claim 25 kinematically (a portion of the ring moves across and in contact with a surface of the poppet during shape recovery) and keep the shearing effect in the description.

findings.title: The axial load path of the purge shoulder is not described and reads against the opening direction
findings.attack: The poppet opens chamber-wards, so a shoulder on the chamber side of the sealing face moves away from the sealing edge and can meet only an undescribed supply-facing ring surface further chamber-wards; the axial order of shoulder 24, edge 34, convolutions and shoulder 44 is never stated, and the retainer of [0116] appears reversed.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a paragraph stating the axial order and the face contacted, taken from the prototype and the inventor sketches, and correct [0116] if it is reversed.

findings.title: The worked-example dimensions do not fit together geometrically
findings.attack: With a mean radius of about 1.25 mm, a 0.12 mm outward crest gives about 2.94 mm outer diameter, which cannot enter a bore sized for 0.03 mm interference on 2.7 mm without an undisclosed relief; an inward trough gives about 2.06 mm inner diameter against an unstated stem diameter.
findings.least_narrowing_action: State the direction of the convolutions, any bore relief over the convoluted length, and the diameter of the poppet stem.

findings.title: Numeral format drift, registry mismatches and claim 100 preamble
findings.attack: Numerals unbracketed in [0030]-[0041] and bracketed thereafter; claim 58 uses (30) where the description uses 730; registry rows 12, 32, 62, 64 do not match the figure instructions; claims 100-102 recite assembly under a seat-ring manufacturing preamble.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Bracket numerals uniformly; claim 58 '(30, 730)'; correct the registry rows; retitle claims 100-102 as a method of manufacturing a valve core.

findings.title: Independent claims require a normal-open state that the description itself says may be absent
findings.attack: [0051] discloses setting the over-travel threshold close to the crack pressure so the purge state is reached on substantially every opening with a single-rate spring; every independent claim requires a normal-open state with an over-travel threshold higher than the crack pressure, so that cheaper variant is outside all of them.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add an independent claim (valve core and method) reciting the closed state and the purge state only, the ring deflected when the poppet is displaced beyond a first displacement and recovering when the differential falls, supported by [0051], [0014], [0065]; keep claim 1 as the three-state claim.

findings.title: Normal-open state requires the ring 'in its at-rest form': escaped by light contact or by a ring-stiffness threshold
findings.attack: A deflecting formation that touches and slightly loads the ring during the normal stroke, without opening the purge gap, removes the 'at-rest form' of the normal-open state, so claims 1, 58 and 79 are not met. The ring-stiffness threshold of [0122] (initial elastic rise before the plateau), and [0050], describe exactly this, making claim 40 arguably fall outside claim 1. [0118] ('not touched') supports the narrow construction. Proof needs micro-CT or sectioning under pressure.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Delete 'the deflectable ring element is in its at-rest form and' from the normal-open state of claims 1, 58 and 79, keeping 'the purge gap is closed' ([0102]). Add a sentence to [0118] and [0122] that the formation may contact and elastically load the ring below the threshold without opening the purge gap, and amend 'is not touched' to 'is not deflected so as to open the purge gap'. Broadening only.

findings.title: Over-travel by mechanical depression is disclosed but no independent claim covers it
findings.attack: A Schrader-pattern core, or a Presta adaptor with a depressor, uses a stiff single-rate spring and reaches over-travel only by depression. Claim 79's 'raising the pressure differential above an over-travel threshold' is never performed. Against claims 1 and 58 the defendant uses [0058] and [0088] (threshold within the device's pressure range) and claim 46's 'additionally' to require a pressure-driven purge in use, forcing the patentee to over-pressurise seized product beyond its rating.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recite the purge state in claims 1 and 58 as reached when the pressure differential exceeds the over-travel threshold or when the poppet is mechanically depressed beyond the normal stroke, or add a parallel independent claim. Add a method claim with depressor-induced or hand-induced over-travel ([0066], [0067], [0137]).

findings.title: Purge state tied to the pressure differential; depressor-actuated and deflation-only purges escape
findings.attack: Claim 1 places the purge state 'at a pressure differential exceeding the over-travel threshold' and claim 79 requires 'raising the pressure differential above an over-travel threshold'; [0066] discloses over-travel by a pump-head depressor 'whatever the pressure differential' and [0067] a deflation-only purge, so a Schrader-style depressor product or a deflation-purge product infringes no independent claim.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Reformulate the purge state in an independent claim by poppet position ('when the poppet is displaced beyond the normal stroke into over-travel'), with the pressure threshold, the depressor and the deflation purge as dependent alternatives; supported by [0012], [0066], [0067].

findings.title: Return spring named in every product claim; a pressure-closed poppet has none
findings.attack: Deleting the spring and closing the poppet by chamber pressure, with the over-travel threshold set by ring stiffness as in [0122], yields a product with every cleaning feature and no 'return spring'; the genus 'biasing member' at [0009] is disclosed only as springs.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recite 'a biasing member' in the independent claims ([0009], [0022]) and add disclosure of a poppet biased closed by chamber-side pressure without a separate spring, threshold set by the ring, subject to inventor confirmation.

findings.title: Seat ring claim 67 limited to Presta-sized rings by numerical ranges in the independent claim
findings.attack: 'a seat ring inner diameter of from 2.0 mm to 2.6 mm and a seat ring wall thickness of from 0.15 mm to 0.30 mm' excludes every Schrader-pattern ring the description contemplates at [0137] and [0091], and a 2.65 mm or 0.32 mm Presta ring; the component claim is the easiest of the five to avoid.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Broaden claim 67 by dropping the ranges, resting on sealing edge, axial-to-radial conversion wall and shape recovery (optionally superelastic alloy), supported by [0034], [0078], [0084], [0091]; keep claims 16, 17, 78 as fallbacks.

findings.title: 'at-rest form' required in the normal-open state; a pre-loaded ring escapes
findings.attack: A purge shoulder that touches and lightly pre-loads the ring at the end of the normal stroke without opening the gap means the ring is not 'in its at-rest form' in the normal-open state; the product behaves identically and the pre-load is below the purge gap opening so is hard to prove either way.
findings.least_narrowing_action: In the normal-open state recite only that the purge gap is closed (and the main passage open), dropping 'at-rest form' there; supported by [0018], [0043]; keep it in the closed state.

findings.title: 'radial deflection' excludes an axially collapsing ring that uncovers an opening
findings.attack: [0079] concedes a wall that 'merely shortens' is outside the mechanism; a bellows-like ring that shortens axially under the shoulder and uncovers a port or lifts a lip axially has no radial deflection and escapes every independent claim.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add disclosure of a deflectable ring element whose over-travel deformation, axial or radial, uncovers the purge opening, if within the inventors' conception; otherwise accept the boundary.

findings.title: Disclosed actuation architectures outside claim 1: separate purge actuator and inverted arrangement
findings.attack: Claim 1 needs the ring 'carried by the core body' and the poppet to 'produce a radial deflection'; [0123] discloses a separate annular piston or diaphragm deflecting the ring while the poppet does only its normal stroke, and [0117] a skirt carried by the poppet deflected by a fixed formation; a Schrader product with a purge piston infringes nothing.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add formulations in which 'a deflecting member movable in response to the pressure differential' produces the deflection (poppet as one species) and in which the ring is carried by the core body or the poppet; supported by [0112], [0117], [0123].

findings.title: Manufacturing claim 90 hidden in the supplier's process and its evidence removed by electropolishing
findings.attack: 'laser cutting' and 'water quenching' are single disclosed species; [0150] discloses roll-forming, internal-pressure forming, etching of sheet and stamping which all escape, and the electropolishing of [0149] removes the heat-affected edge that would evidence laser cutting; the process is performed abroad and undetectable from the product.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Reformulate to 'cutting a profile of the seat ring from tube stock or from sheet' ([0150]); generalising the quench requires new disclosure; counsel to weigh whether claim 90 earns its examination cost.

findings.title: Manufacturing claim 90 is hidden in the factory and escaped by changing the quench or the cutting route
findings.attack: The process is performed abroad and electropolishing removes the laser trace ([0149]). Air or oil cooling escapes 'water quenching', and photochemical etching or stamping escapes 'laser cutting' ([0150]). Product-by-process protection for imports presupposes proof of the process.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Delete 'and then water quenching' from claim 90 (kept in claim 94). Make laser cutting one alternative for producing the profile and put it in a dependent claim ([0147], [0148], [0150]). Counsel to weigh the EPO intermediate-generalisation risk.

findings.title: Method claim 79 performed by the user and requires proof of sealant film on the accused surfaces
findings.attack: Every step is performed by the cyclist so the competitor is reached only by indirect infringement; 'across surfaces on which sealant film accumulates' makes infringement depend on the condition of the accused valve at the time of use and requires proof of film on those surfaces.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recite 'across a surface of the deflectable ring element' ([0056]) in claim 79 and move 'on which sealant film accumulates' to a dependent claim; ensure product claims carry every structural feature the method relies on.

findings.title: Only radial, in-place deformation is covered: axial flexing or bodily displacement of the ring escapes
findings.attack: A diaphragm ring that flexes out of plane to lift a lip from an axial face, or a rigid ring pushed axially off a land to uncover flutes, opens a purge path only in over-travel without any 'radial deflection' as defined in [0020]. The bodily displaced form lies near refs. #13 and #16.
findings.least_narrowing_action: If within conception, add an embodiment in which elastic out-of-plane flexure of the ring opens the purge gap, and claim 'elastic deformation of the deflectable ring element' without 'radial'. Do not claim bodily displacement unless counsel is satisfied on refs. #13 and #16.

findings.title: Purge gap 'closed' in the closed and normal-open states; a permanent small downstream clearance escapes
findings.attack: A purge gap on the chamber side of the sealing edge ([0105]) can carry a permanent measurable clearance without leaking the tyre; such a gap is never 'closed', and [0105]'s 'sufficiently small to carry no significant flow' wording applies only to that one location, not to the generic definition at [0018].
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a generic sentence to [0018] that the purge gap is 'closed' when closed or carrying no significant flow relative to the main passage, extending [0105] to every location, and rely on it in the claims.

findings.title: Seat ring claim 67 is avoided by leaving the dimensional window, or by a wall convoluted along its whole length
findings.attack: A Schrader-scale ring, an inner diameter of 2.65 mm, a wall of 0.32 mm, a FIG. 12 wall, or a wall convoluted end to end (no 'portion of the wall free of convolutions' at which to measure under [0028]) escapes claim 67. Replacement rings outside the window are free.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a fallback measurement convention to [0028] (for example, the diameter at the sealing edge (34) where no portion is free of convolutions). Consider an independent seat-ring claim without dimensions (sealing edge for a poppet, convoluted wall, superelastic alloy), with the ranges as dependents, subject to counsel's view on ref. #1. The current claim gives up every non-Presta-scale ring.

findings.title: Separate purge actuator and inverted arrangement escape 'the poppet ... produces a radial deflection' and 'carried by the core body'
findings.attack: With the purge actuator of [0123] the poppet performs only its normal stroke, so no purge state as claimed exists. With the inverted skirt-on-poppet arrangement of [0117], 'carried by the core body' depends on a contested indirect-carriage reading of [0005].
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recite the deflection as produced by a deflecting formation moved by the poppet in over-travel or by a purge actuator responsive to the pressure differential exceeding the over-travel threshold ([0123]), and the ring as carried by the core body or by the poppet ([0117]).

findings.title: Shape recovery 'to its at-rest form' and tied to the over-travel threshold
findings.attack: [0099] admits residual set after many cycles; a competitor shows its cycled ring does not return 'to' the at-rest form, and a ring whose gap closes only below the crack pressure argues it does not close 'when the pressure differential falls below the over-travel threshold'.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recite 'shape recovery towards its at-rest form and closing the purge gap when the pressure differential falls', tracking [0013] and [0014].

findings.title: Supply of seat ring, poppet and return spring as a kit, or of core parts to a stem maker, avoids claim 1
findings.attack: Claim 1 requires 'a core body (20)'. A matched kit of ring, poppet and spring for assembly into someone else's core body, or parts shipped to a stem maker, is not a direct infringement. Indirect infringement needs knowledge, and claim 67 catches only rings inside its window.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a kit claim: deflectable ring element, poppet with sealing face and deflecting formation, and return spring, matched so that on assembly the closed, normal-open and purge states of claim 1 result ([0141], FIG. 5).

findings.title: 'return spring' is the species; the package defines the genus 'biasing member'
findings.attack: A non-spring bias invites the argument that the plain meaning of 'spring' prevails over [0022].
findings.least_narrowing_action: Use 'a biasing member (50)' in the independent claims ([0009], [0022]).

findings.title: 'separate from the main passage' invites a construction fight where the flows merge
findings.attack: Where the purge flow runs along the poppet stem ([0105]), the defendant argues that the purge path is not 'separate' from the main passage.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recite the purge gap as a flow path distinct from the main passage and opened only by the radial deflection, locating the separation at the gap ([0019], [0045], [0102]).

findings.title: Method of operating claim 79 is performed by the end user
findings.attack: The cyclist is the direct infringer. A competitor is liable only for inducement or contributory infringement (knowledge and intent), or under UK s.60(2), and the claim is confined by [0025] to bicycle chambers holding sealant.
findings.least_narrowing_action: No change required. Keep the product claims free of in-use requirements, and carry the fixes for F-33-1 and F-33-2 into claim 79.

findings.title: Product claim 25 recites a result in use: 'shears sealant film'
findings.attack: An unused core has no film to shear, so proof needs used product and evidence of shearing that the package concedes is not separately measured.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recite the movement alone ('moves across a surface of the poppet'), which [0124] makes definitive, and keep 'shears sealant film' in method claim 80.

findings.title: Claim 67 scores 3 for design-around resistance
findings.attack: A Schrader-scale ring, a ring just outside either range, a FIG. 12 wall, or a wall with no convolution-free portion for the [0028] measurement escapes, leaving the replacement-seat-ring channel of [0141] free.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a fallback measurement convention to [0028]. Consider an independent seat-ring claim without dimensions (sealing edge for a poppet, convoluted wall, superelastic alloy) with the ranges as dependents, subject to counsel's view on index #1.

findings.title: Claim 90 scores 2 for design-around resistance and 2 for detectability
findings.attack: Changing the quench medium or cutting route escapes 'laser cutting' and 'then water quenching'. The process runs abroad and electropolishing removes its trace ([0149]), so the claim adds almost no moat.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Delete 'and then water quenching' (kept in claim 94) and recite laser cutting as one alternative with a dependent claim ([0147], [0148], [0150]). Counsel to weigh the EPO intermediate-generalisation risk.

findings.title: Claims 1 and 58 score 5 for design-around resistance: four disclosed escape architectures are unclaimed
findings.attack: The description discloses the two-state single-rate-spring variant ([0051]), the depressor-actuated purge ([0066]), the separate purge actuator ([0123]) and the inverted ring-on-poppet arrangement ([0117]); none is inside an independent claim, which requires a normal-open state, a return spring and poppet-produced radial deflection.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add an independent claim to the closed and purge states only, purge state defined by displacement of a deflecting member beyond a first displacement, ring carried by the core body or the poppet, and 'a biasing member' for the spring; supported by [0009], [0022], [0051], [0066], [0112], [0117], [0123].

findings.title: Method claim 79 scores 4 for detectability and 4 for evidentiary ease
findings.attack: Every step is the user's act; proof of 'an air purge ... across surfaces on which sealant film accumulates' needs the accused valve after use with sealant, a bench rig and evidence that the user's pump exceeded the threshold, which [0179] concedes hand pumps and CO2 devices may not.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Recite 'across a surface of the deflectable ring element' ([0056]) in place of the sealant-film condition; carry every structural precondition into claims 1 and 58; keep claim 79 as the inducement vehicle.

findings.title: Seat ring claim 67 scores 3 for design-around resistance because of numerical ranges and the convoluted-wall limitation
findings.attack: 'a seat ring inner diameter of from 2.0 mm to 2.6 mm and a seat ring wall thickness of from 0.15 mm to 0.30 mm' and 'a convoluted wall (32)' exclude every Schrader-pattern ring, any Presta ring marginally outside the ranges, and the frustoconical, slotted and cellular walls of [0081]; an aftermarket ring supplier avoids the only component claim at no engineering cost.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Broaden claim 67 to the sealing edge, the axial-to-radial conversion wall (claim 10 wording, [0078]) and shape recovery, adding the superelastic alloy of claim 73 if novelty needs it; keep ranges and convoluted wall as dependents.

findings.title: Claim 79 scores 4 for design-around resistance
findings.attack: An adaptor with a depressor produces over-travel without 'raising the pressure differential above an over-travel threshold'; a pump below the threshold produces no purge at all.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a method claim with over-travel produced by mechanical depression during coupling ([0066], [0067]).

findings.title: Load path of the purge shoulder and through-route of the purge flow past the retention band not stated for the illustrated embodiment
findings.attack: The description never states which end of the seat ring carries the sealing edge relative to the internal shoulder, which ring surface the purge shoulder (on the chamber side of the sealing face, moving in the opening direction) bears on, or how gas in the annular outer-surface purge gap passes the interference band that seats the ring against the internal shoulder; the registry's flag 3 concedes the FIG. 6 convention is a drafting assumption, so sufficiency and clarity of claim 1's through-flow for the FIG. 1 embodiment are exposed.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add to [0034], [0038] and [0056] a plain statement of the axial arrangement and of the route by which the purge flow enters the annular purge gap at the supply side and leaves at the chamber side (past the free end and the freed region, or via purge ports 262 or flutes 362), taken from the inventor's sketches.

findings.title: No drawings exist: the package holds a figure plan that contains internal working references
findings.attack: The description relies on FIGs. 1-15, but the package holds only a figure plan and draftsperson instructions. Filing without drawings risks re-dating (EPC R. 56) or loss of the figure references, and the US requires drawings where necessary (35 USC 113). The plan text contains internal references ('01 Q22', 'DA-7', 'Assumption A2 in Prompt 20') that must not be filed.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Produce FIGs. 1-15 from registry.md (after F-36-1 for FIGs. 1, 3, 6 and 10), complete the deferred numeral cross-check, add a Brief Description of the Drawings, and exclude all figure-plan working text from the filing.

findings.title: Wipe-only embodiment of [0065] has no claim family
findings.attack: [0065] discloses cleaning 'by the snap-back wipe alone, the deflectable ring element being sealed at its periphery so that no inflation gas flows past it'; claim 25 depends on claim 1 which requires the purge gap and purge flow path, so a sealed-periphery deflectable seat ring that snaps back across the sealing face infringes nothing while getting the benefit [0167] attributes to the wiped surfaces.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add an independent valve core claim to the deflectable ring element carrying the sealing edge, deflected by the poppet in over-travel and moving across the sealing face on shape recovery, without the purge gap (purge gap dependent), plus a corresponding method claim and a figure of the sealed-periphery form; supported by [0061], [0065], [0092], FIG. 4.

findings.title: 'Inflatable chamber' is defined as bicycle-only; sealant-filled e-scooter, motorcycle and other tyres are left out
findings.attack: The [0025] definition confines claims 58 and 79 to bicycle chambers, so an e-scooter or motorcycle tubeless valve with the mechanism argues non-infringement. [0139] gives only a general sentence as basis for later amendment.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Redefine the inflatable chamber as any tyre or inner tube inflated through the valve and holding liquid sealant, with bicycle chambers as the tested example, and name the other contemplated chambers.

findings.title: Behaviour on top-up inflation is not described
findings.attack: Every tested event ran from fully deflated to 6 bar; on a top-up from riding pressure the differential across the open poppet is the flow-induced drop, not the gauge pressure, and the package does not say whether the 3.5 bar threshold is reached on a floor-pump stroke into a pressurised chamber, while [0068] states the cleaning actions occur 'once per inflation event'.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a paragraph after [0069] stating whether and on what basis the purge state is reached on top-up inflation, and that the tested event is inflation from fully deflated; if unknown, say so in the manner of [0165].

findings.title: Claimed and disclosed features without a figure
findings.attack: Claims 24, 28, 31, 32, 45 and 46, and the unclaimed retainer/sleeve, conical disc, purge actuator, inverted arrangement, wiping land, helical wipe and wipe-only forms appear in no figure; 37 CFR 1.83(a) requires claimed features to be shown and a post-filing figure cannot add matter, and at the EPO and UK an undrawn alternative is the first called an unsupported generalisation.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add schematic partial sections in the style of FIGs. 11–14 for the claimed features at least and for the wipe-only and purge-actuator forms; the description already gives the structure.

findings.title: How the band-limited interference fit is made is not disclosed
findings.attack: Claim 21 and four paragraphs recite an interference over an axial band with the remainder clear, but none says whether that is by a relief in the bore, a reduced outer diameter on the ring's free portion, or a step, and the ring is drawn from plain 2.7 mm tube; the registry's flag 3 concedes the convention is a drafting assumption.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add one sentence at [0036] stating the means (bore relief, ring relief, or both) and, if known, the axial length of the band, after inventor confirmation.

findings.title: No claims to non-bicycle sealant-holding chambers, to the kit, or to the inflation system with a depressor head
findings.attack: Claims 64–66 are limited to bicycle chambers; [0139] extends the mechanism to other sealant-holding chambers, [0141] discloses the seat ring kit and [0066] the depressor head or adaptor, none of which is claimed and none of which can be added after filing.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a chamber claim generic to an inflatable chamber holding liquid sealant with bicycle forms dependent, a kit claim per [0141], and an inflation system claim (valve plus device head or adaptor with a depressor sized to move the poppet into over-travel) per [0066].

findings.title: No embodiment opens the purge path by out-of-plane (axial) flexure of the ring
findings.attack: A diaphragm ring flexing axially to lift a lip opens a purge path only in over-travel and escapes every claim reciting 'radial deflection'.
findings.least_narrowing_action: If within conception, add the embodiment and a generic statement that the elastic deformation opening the purge gap may be radial or axial.

findings.title: No embodiment purges from first lift (zero normal stroke)
findings.attack: Every independent claim requires a normal-open state. A product purging from first lift has none, and [0051] discloses only a short normal stroke, so there is no basis for a claim family without it.
findings.least_narrowing_action: If within conception, add an embodiment with the purge gap opening as the poppet lifts (single-rate spring, no normal stroke) and an independent claim without the normal-open state, with counsel weighing index #14 and #16.

findings.title: No generic definition of a 'closed' purge gap and no tolerance on 'at-rest form'
findings.attack: [0018] says the purge gap is 'closed' and [0105] gives the 'no significant flow' test for one location only; claims recite recovery 'to its at-rest form' while [0013] says 'towards' and [0099] admits residual set; strict construction gives two escapes and support for a cure at one location only.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add to [0018] that the purge gap is closed when closed or carrying no significant flow relative to the main passage, for every location, and to [0013] that shape recovery is return towards the at-rest form sufficient to close the purge gap, residual set notwithstanding.

findings.title: No ranges for the normal stroke, the rest clearance of the purge shoulder, or the spring-stage rate ratio
findings.attack: The normal stroke is a single value (0.6 mm), the rest clearance has no value and the second-stage rate is only 'higher'; the parameters a competitor's core will differ in have no numeric fallback, and [0088] supports only a qualitative amendment.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add ranges for the normal stroke, the rest clearance (at least the normal stroke plus a margin) and the ratio of second to first spring-stage rate, bracketing the tested values, as ranges within which the mechanism is expected to operate in the manner of [0006] and [0088].

findings.title: Over-travel by a depressor has no geometry or control logic
findings.attack: There is no relation between depressor travel, normal stroke and over-travel distance, and no account of how a Schrader core, whose pin every head depresses, keeps a normal-open state. The Schrader and adaptor variants, and any claim built on [0066], are exposed on enablement and support.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the depressor geometry (travel exceeding the normal stroke plus a stated fraction of the over-travel distance) and the Schrader variant's operating sequence.

findings.title: The cheapest competitor combination is disclosed only by a blanket combination statement
findings.attack: A moulded polymer core body with an integral flexure, a single-rate spring with a stiffness-set threshold, and moulded flutes is the lowest-cost competitor product. The [0143] blanket statement is weak EPO basis for selecting that combination from several lists.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a written prophetic embodiment of this combination, including how the threshold is set without a second spring stage.

findings.title: The package contradicts itself on whether the ring is touched below the over-travel threshold
findings.attack: [0118] says the ring is 'not touched' below the threshold, while [0122] sets the threshold by the force to deflect the ring after an initial elastic rise, which requires contact below it. Claim 40 read with claim 1's normal-open 'at-rest form' lacks support and clarity, and [0118] fixes a narrow construction.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add control logic that the formation may contact and elastically load the ring below the threshold with the purge gap still closed, amend [0118] to 'is not deflected so as to open the purge gap', and align claim 1 as in F-33-1.

findings.title: Two-state, depressor-actuated and deflation-only operating modes have no independent claim
